hints: Evaluate at $x = 4$ to find gradient $\frac{3}{8}$, then write tangent through $(4, 4)$.
walkthrough:
Find the coordinates of point $A$ at $x = 4$:
$$y = \sqrt{3(4) + 4} = \sqrt{16} = 4 \implies A = (4, 4)$$

Differentiate $y = (3x + 4)^{1/2}$ with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2}(3x + 4)^{-1/2} \times (3) = \frac{3}{2\sqrt{3x + 4}}$$

Write the equation of the tangent line through $A(4, 4)$:
$$y - 4 = \frac{3}{8}(x - 4) \implies y = \frac{3}{8}x - \frac{3}{2} + 4 \implies y = \frac{3}{8}x + \frac{5}{2}$$

hints: Calculate area under tangent (trapezium) from $0$ to $4$: $\frac{1}{2}(4)(2.5 + 4) = 13$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area under the straight tangent line $y = \frac{3}{8}x + \frac{5}{2}$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 4$ (trapezium):
$$\text{Area}_{\text{line}} = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times \left( \frac{5}{2} + 4 \right) = 2 \times \frac{13}{2} = 13$$

Evaluate the definite integral for the area under the curve from $x = 0$ to $x = 4$:
$$\text{Area}_{\text{curve}} = \int_0^4 (3x + 4)^{1/2}\,dx = \left[ \frac{(3x + 4)^{3/2}}{\frac{3}{2} \times 3} \right]_0^4 = \left[ \frac{2}{9}(3x + 4)^{3/2} \right]_0^4$$
$$\text{Area}_{\text{curve}} = \frac{2}{9}(16^{3/2} - 4^{3/2}) = \frac{2}{9}(64 - 8) = \frac{2}{9}(56) = \frac{112}{9} = 12\frac{4}{9}$$

Subtract the area under the curve from the area under the tangent line:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = 13 - \frac{112}{9} = \frac{117 - 112}{9} = \frac{5}{9} \quad (\approx 0.556)$$

Use the given connected rate relation $\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}\frac{dx}{dt}$ to determine the gradient at $P$:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} = \frac{1}{2}$$

Equate the derivative expression to $\frac{1}{2}$ and solve for $x$:
$$\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3x + 4}} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \frac{3}{\sqrt{3x + 4}} = 1$$
$$\sqrt{3x + 4} = 3 \implies 3x + 4 = 9$$
$$3x = 5 \implies x = \frac{5}{3} \quad \left(\text{or } 1\frac{2}{3}\right)$$
